title: The ninth: Arafah
hook: standing on the plain from noon to sunset: Hajj is Arafah (Tirmidhi)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the eighth, at Mina, and your line: a city of tents. Who did you share a small space with? Day one thousand one hundred thirty-one.

A group of travelers arrives at the plain of Arafah and finds the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ there. They have one question: what is the Hajj? A man is sent to call out his answer to the crowd, and it's short. The Hajj is Arafah. The report, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mar, is in the collection of Tirmidhi. All the rest, the cloths, the circling, the walking, the tents, leads to this one day. Today, the ninth.
screen: `TRAVELERS WITH ONE QUESTION.` → `WHAT IS THE HAJJ?` → `THE HAJJ IS ARAFAH.`

segments.voice: First, the word. Wuquf means standing, and it's the name for being present on the plain of Arafah on the ninth day. Tirmidhi's report goes on: whoever reaches Arafah before dawn after that night has caught the Hajj. Miss it, and in the teaching of the scholars the Hajj itself is missed, whatever else was done. Second, what the Prophet did. Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says he left Mina after sunrise, and when the sun passed its height, he addressed the people, then the noon and afternoon prayers were prayed together. Then he rode to the place of standing, faced the qiblah, and stayed there, still on his camel, until the sun had set. Noon to sunset. That's the shape of the day. Third, what standing means. It doesn't require being on your feet. Pilgrims sit under umbrellas, stand by the roadside, rest in tents, lift their hands, read the Qur'an, cry, say nothing at all. The rite is being there, turned toward God, for those hours. Fourth, why this day. Aisha reports, in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet saying that there is no day on which Allah sets free more servants from the Fire than the day of Arafah. So the plain fills with people asking, for themselves, for their parents, for names written on scraps of paper by people at home. Then, at sunset, the whole crowd moves at once. The Qur'an, in surah two, gives the instruction for that moment in Pickthall's words: "But, when ye press on in the multitude from 'Arafat, remember Allah by the sacred monument." That's where tomorrow begins.
screen: `WUQUF: STANDING, BEING THERE.` · `FROM NOON TO SUNSET.` · `ON YOUR FEET OR NOT.` · `NO DAY FREES MORE SERVANTS.`

segments.voice: The practice: stand in du'a. Pilgrims give a whole afternoon to it; an hour is a generous start at home. The bell gives two minutes, so begin there, and keep going after it if you like. Stand, or sit if standing is hard. Turn your palms up. If you pray, ask, in your own words, for yourself and then for someone else by name. If you don't, hold in mind what you most hope for, and then one person you hope it for too. The bell holds the time.
Wuquf. Standing on the plain of Arafah, from noon to sunset on the ninth, the heart of the Hajj. Today's word.
Your line: hajj is arafah. Today, find the one part of a task that everything else depends on, and give it your best hour. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: On the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah, pilgrims go from Mina to the plain of Arafah, pray the noon and afternoon prayers together, and spend the afternoon until sunset in du'a, recitation and remembrance before moving on to Muzdalifah.

notes: Tirmidhi 889 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'mar: people of Najd asked; 'the Hajj is Arafah'; whoever comes before dawn on the night of Jam' has caught it): confirm number and grading. The report calls them people of Najd; the script says 'a group of travelers'.
'Miss it, and in the teaching of the scholars the Hajj itself is missed': standard fiqh; confirm phrasing.
Sahih Muslim 1218 (Jabir: sermon after the sun declined, zuhr and asr together, then standing facing the qiblah until sunset): confirm.
Sahih Muslim 1348 (Aisha: no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than the day of Arafah): paraphrased; confirm.
Pickthall 2:198 quoted from memory, including the spelling 'Arafat: confirm exact wording.
'Names written on scraps of paper by people at home' and the list of how pilgrims spend the afternoon: general color; check.
Practice adapts the outline's 'stand in du'a for an hour' to the two-minute sit, inviting the listener to continue.
